issue.title: Diagnose the race between agents-sync publication and workspace-prep clean/reset against the shared agents sidecar clone
issue.description: Root-cause the race that emptied the sase agents-repo owner manifest from 1389 hoods to 1 hood in a single publication: agents-repo commit 5f244a229 (2026-08-06 09:11:53, 1389 hoods) -> 6ad0b6e2a (2026-08-06 09:16:12, 1 hood, 'tv' only), with the commit's diff losing the manifest entries plus 1390 lines of the browsing README. 6ad0b6e2a is the exact fetched_sha recorded in five stale incoming-cache items that misclassified this machine's own 24 legacy-v1 runs as an unknown-user import (surfaced as a green unknown-user badge in ACE). The agents-repo reflog shows a whole-tree 'reset: moving to HEAD' + 'checkout: moving from main to main' one second before that commit (2026-08-06 09:16:11) -- the signature of vcs_clean_workspace (git reset --hard HEAD + git clean -fd) followed by a branch checkout, i.e. a workspace-preparation pass running against the agents sidecar clone at ~/.sase/projects/gh_sase-org__sase/repos/agents, which all 24 sase_<N> workspaces share. The 1391 hood directories under users/bbugyi200/machines/athena/hoods/ survived intact -- only the manifest.json that references them was truncated, meaning publication_planning.plan_hoods's read_owner_manifest() must have seen a missing or freshly-reset manifest.json (v2_manifest_io.read_owner_manifest returns an empty V2OwnerManifest when the file is not present) and then republished from that empty base for a single targeted hood ('tv'), overwriting the real manifest. The precise interleaving that made the file unreadable at that instant -- whether the clean/reset briefly deleted manifest.json while a concurrent publish read it, or checkout raced a write, or something else entirely -- is not diagnosed. Discovered and surfaced via plan sase/repos/plans/202608/unknown_user_legacy_hood_ownership.md, whose Fix 3/Fix 4 (landed in that plan's implementation) harden publication_planning.plan_hoods to raise AgentsSyncFormatError instead of silently republishing from an empty manifest when on-disk hood directories exist, and add a 'sase agent sync --repair-manifest' command to reconstruct lost manifest entries from intact on-disk snapshots -- but those are containment/repair, not a fix for the underlying race. A related precedent exists: sase-ab.1 (closed) solved an analogous problem for the *beads* sidecar, teaching workspace-preparation to protect or publish local-only bead-store commits before a clean+hard checkout discards them; that fix's shape (protect-before-clean) may be a useful starting point but does not itself cover the agents sidecar's manifest.json, since sase-ab.1 was scoped to bead-store commit protection only. Scope: reproduce or trace the concurrent-workspace-preparation-vs-agents-sync-publication interleaving against the shared agents sidecar clone, and land whichever fix shape avoids the corruption at its source (e.g. per-workspace clones instead of a shared one, a lock that workspace-prep's clean/reset respects, or protecting/publishing local-only agents-sidecar commits before a hard reset the way sase-ab.1 did for beads).
